title: Staged failover ceremony and consistency assertion orchestrator
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Purpose: create an opinionated, repeatable "ceremony" for scheduled active->passive rehearsals that combines an automated consistency assertion harness with operational choreography so we can validate backup fidelity, KV resync behavior, and SLO gating before traffic cutover. Background: We have regular DR drills but lack a single orchestrator that enforces SLO gates, toggles circuit-breaker overrides, and runs checksum-based snapshot comparisons as part of the exercise. This ticket builds the lightweight Orchestrator (Python lambda + Step Function prototype), the assertion tooling for backup/restore verification, and an on-call choreography guide for the human steps. Goals: 1) Run a scheduled staged failover drill that moves a subset of traffic to passive region behind a temporary circuit-breaker, 2) Validate backup/restore integrity via checksum and record-level reconciliation with tolerances, 3) Gate promotion on SLO and validation pass/fail criteria, 4) Provide clear rollback paths and post-drill artifacts (diffs, dashboards, PRs) for engineering review.
acceptance_criteria: Orchestrator can be triggered by schedule or manually via Console and records a unique drill run id
During a drill, system applies a temporary circuit-breaker to route 10% -> 100% to passive region according to staged schedule
Validation harness completes backup restore verification with pass/fail flags within 30 minutes of restore completion
SLO gate (p99 <= configured threshold and error rate < configured threshold) must be evaluated; if gate fails, orchestrator aborts promotion and re-routes traffic back
Run artifacts (snapshot checksums, reconciliation report, timeline of actions, dashboard links) are uploaded to the drill run object and linked in the ticket
Post-drill automated smoke tests confirm API parity for 20 representative endpoints and surface diffs for KV count deltas
runbook_steps: Pre-flight: Verify run id generated and snapshot job completed for primary region; ensure snapshot checksum published to S3 and stored in metadata table
Step 1 (Warmup): Start passive region warmup; prepopulate caches with prefix caching keys for common prompt prefixes; verify latency < baseline+30ms
Step 2 (Circuit breaker): Apply staged circuit-breaker policy (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with progressive hold times; monitor for error spikes
Step 3 (Traffic siphon): Use traffic-siphon service to mirror requests to passive region for live validation (non-invasive) before promotion
Step 4 (Restore): Trigger restore of latest snapshot to passive region; run snapshot-checksum-compare tool against source snapshot
Step 5 (Consistency assertion): Run record-level reconciliation (sampled) with tolerance thresholds and KV reconciliation report generated
Step 6 (SLO gating): Run SLO queries (p95/p99 latency, error rate, token throughput) for both regions; if any metric breaches configured threshold, abort promotion and trigger rollback
Step 7 (Promotion): If gates pass, proceed with staged promotion to passive; increment traffic according to schedule; continue to monitor
Step 8 (Smoke): Run 20 canonical smoke requests including chat generation, long-context continuation, and embeddings; compare outputs for structural parity
Step 9 (Tear down): Revert circuit-breaker and traffic routing back to primary after test window or keep promoted if validated and approved
Step 10 (Postmortem): Collect logs, reconciliation artifacts, SLO graphs, and open follow-up actions within 48 hours
telemetry_queries: KV delta query (BigQuery): SELECT COUNTIF(modified_time > restore_time AND NOT EXISTS_in_primary) as orphan_count, COUNTIF(primary_count != restore_count) as mismatched_count FROM kv_reconciliation WHERE run_id = '{{run_id}}'
Snapshot checksum validation (SQL): SELECT snapshot_id, checksum FROM snapshot_metadata WHERE region = 'primary' AND created_at = '{{snapshot_time}}'
Traffic split verification: SELECT percentile(latency_ms, 99) FROM latency_logs WHERE region = 'passive' AND timestamp > '{{promotion_time}}'
rollback_plan: If SLO gate fails or reconciliation mismatches exceed tolerances: 1) Immediately apply emergency routing to primary (circuit-breaker open for passive), 2) Drain passive in-flight requests via quiesce API, 3) If tokenstore locks were acquired, release fences and run tokenstore integrity check, 4) Mark run as failed and attach reconciliation artifacts for postmortem. Operators should use the Orchestrator abort endpoint which will run automated rollback steps and annotate the run with a failure reason.
validation_harness_spec: Checksum comparator: SHA256 of each snapshot file compared between primary and restored snapshot; differences logged and sampled files extracted for forensic analysis
Record sampler: Deterministic sampling (hash mod 1000 == run_id mod 1000) of keys for record-level verification to keep compute bounded
KV reconciliation rules: tolerate <0.1% key-count delta and <0.05% differing records for non-critical namespaces; fail on any delta for identity/metadata namespaces
Synthetic replay: Replay captured 1k requests (sanitized) against passive and compare response shape, status codes, and token counts; differences classified as minor/major
Artifacts: Produce a single reconciliaton-report.json and an artifacts bundle (logs + checksums) uploaded to S3 with signed URL in the drill run
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Snapshot restore may take longer than expected and push passive region capacity; Mitigation: Pre-reserve warm standby capacity and run a dry-run restore during maintenance window
Risk: Circuit-breaker misconfiguration could route too much traffic too quickly; Mitigation: Use progressive ramping with conservative defaults and auto-abort on SLO divergence
Risk: False positives in record-level reconciliation due to eventual consistency; Mitigation: Use bounded sampling window and mark certain namespaces as eventually-consistent with relaxed thresholds
Risk: On-call fatigue if drills are too frequent; Mitigation: Limit automated drills to monthly with opt-in extra rehearsals for critical customers
